title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 6 (Revocation how made)

content.overview: Section 6 provides that a proposal is revoked — (1) by the communication of notice of revocation by the proposer to the other party; (2) by the lapse of the time prescribed in such proposal for its acceptance, or, if no time is so prescribed, by the lapse of a reasonable time, without communication of the acceptance; (3) by the failure of the acceptor to fulfil a condition precedent to acceptance; or (4) by the death or insanity of the proposer, if the fact of his death or insanity comes to the knowledge of the acceptor before acceptance.
content.glance: Four modes: notice; lapse of prescribed/reasonable time; failure of condition precedent; death/insanity known before acceptance.
content.study: A proposal is revoked by (1) communication of notice of revocation to the other party; (2) lapse of the time prescribed for acceptance, or of a reasonable time if none is prescribed, without communication of acceptance; (3) failure of the acceptor to fulfil a condition precedent to acceptance; or (4) death or insanity of the proposer if that fact comes to the acceptor’s knowledge before acceptance. Timing of communication of revocation is under ss. 3–4; the window for revocation is under s. 5. Current-law framing: identify which mode applies; apply communication rules; conclude whether the proposal still stands.

sections.heading: Notice of revocation
sections.body: Communication of notice of revocation by the proposer to the other party.

sections.heading: Lapse of time
sections.body: Lapse of the time prescribed for acceptance, or of a reasonable time if none is prescribed, without communication of acceptance.

sections.heading: Failure of condition precedent
sections.body: Failure of the acceptor to fulfil a condition precedent to acceptance.

sections.heading: Death or insanity of proposer
sections.body: Death or insanity of the proposer if the fact comes to the acceptor’s knowledge before acceptance.

examples.title: Lapse of reasonable time
examples.body: No time is fixed for acceptance. A reasonable time passes without acceptance. The proposal is revoked under s. 6(2).

hypotheticals.question: Does the proposer’s death always revoke the proposal?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only if the fact of death (or insanity) comes to the acceptor’s knowledge before acceptance — s. 6(4).

distinctions.title: Modes of revocation (s. 6) vs timing window (s. 5)
distinctions.right: Until when revocation is still open

misconceptions.trap: Death of the proposer automatically ends every outstanding proposal even if the offeree never learns of it before accepting.
misconceptions.correction: Section 6(4) requires that the fact of death or insanity come to the acceptor’s knowledge before acceptance.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 6 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the mode of revocation. II. Apply communication rules (ss. 3–4) where notice is involved. III. Apply s. 5 for the timing window. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Stress knowledge of death/insanity before acceptance.
